616390260/daletou-predictor.body:
# Daletou Prediction Lab

Current experiments include a nine-model per-draw comparison, an independent Laya review, and a [winning-coverage experiment](https://github.com/616390260/daletou-predictor/blob/HEAD/docs/PORTFOLIO.md) with a fixed stake of nine bets for 18 yuan. Theoretical coverage, historical simulations, and results published before the actual draw are displayed separately; prizes and ROI are rule-based estimates.

[2026-10-16 retraining log](https://github.com/616390260/daletou-predictor/blob/HEAD/docs/RETRAINING_2026-10-16.md): LSTM, Transformer, and XGBoost have been fully retrained on corrected data through draw 26117. The 60-draw isolated validation has not yet outperformed the uniform-probability baseline.

A small experiment to **expose the illusion that "lottery can be predicted by algorithms"**.

Five models with different approaches (random baseline, frequency statistics, Markov chain, LSTM neural network, genetic algorithm) predict Daletou numbers in parallel, generating 4 bets per draw. After each draw, their long-term hit rates and return on investment are compared head-to-head.

---

## Core ideas

- **The lottery is truly random**, so any model's long-term hit rate should **converge to the random baseline**
- The purpose of this platform is **not to "predict winning numbers"**, but to:
  - Test claims such as "hot and cold numbers", "number memory", and "neural networks can capture patterns"
  - Provide a **fair long-term benchmark** so that the methods of various "gurus" can be quantitatively tested
  - Walk through the complete pipeline of **data scraping → modeling → backtesting → visualization → automation**

## Architecture

```
Data flow
  ├── China Sports Lottery official API
  ├── SQLite (data/daletou.db)
  ├── 5 prediction models
  └── Export JSON → Vue3 frontend → GitHub Pages

Scheduled tasks (GitHub Actions)
  ├── Mon/Wed/Sat 18:00 Beijing time → generate next-draw predictions
  └── Mon/Wed/Sat 22:30 Beijing time → fetch draw results + evaluate + redeploy frontend
```

## Directory structure

```
DaLeTou/
├── backend/                 # Python backend
│   ├── requirements.txt
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── config.py        # lottery rules / prize table / model list, etc.
│   │   ├── db/              # SQLite access
│   │   ├── scraper/         # historical data scraper
│   │   ├── models/          # 5 prediction models
│   │   ├── tasks/           # prediction / evaluation / backtesting
│   │   ├──…

Chyona/live-mixer.body:
# Live Stream Clipping Workbench

[Chinese](https://github.com/Chyona/live-mixer/blob/HEAD/README.md) · [English](https://github.com/Chyona/live-mixer/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

> **AI-assisted live stream clipping tool** · Speech recognition · Smart segment selection · CapCut drafts · One-click video output  
> Repository technical name: `live-mixer` · Helps live streaming operations and editing teams greatly improve clipping efficiency

Tech stack: Go 1.25+ · PostgreSQL 14+ · Docker Compose · See LICENSE in the repository

---

## Online Demo Environment

> **Demo: [https://gogoshine.com](https://gogoshine.com)**
>
> No local deployment required. Open your browser to try the full live stream clipping workbench: material ingestion, ASR transcription, AI clipping, CapCut drafts, and one-click video output.

---

## Why Choose the Live Stream Clipping Workbench?

An end-to-end clipping pipeline for **live stream replays / recordings**: from material ingestion, ASR transcription, and AI-driven segment selection to CapCut drafts and final video export, all in one connected flow. It supports "fully automatic one-click output" as well as a collaborative "AI rough selection + manual refinement" mode, handing repetitive work to the model while keeping final quality in human hands.

**Who it's for**

- Live e-commerce, paid knowledge, gaming, and entertainment teams that need to produce clips frequently
- Creators and editors who want to use large models to speed up "listening to transcripts and selecting segments," then finish post-production packaging in CapCut
- R&D teams that need a self-hostable, privately deployable live stream clipping / remix backend service

---

## Core Capabilities

| Capability | Description |
|------|------|
| Live material management | Import replay / recording URLs (files or m3u8), automatically detect resolution and duration |
| Speech recognition (ASR) | Asynchronous transcription, outputs sentence segmentation, summaries, and paragraph structure; subtitles can be downloaded |
| Editing projects | Associate materials and system prompts; maintain rough selection intervals `clips0` and refined segments `clips1` |
| AI live clipping | Based on prompts and rough selection intervals, filter high-value sentences from ASR and write them back to `clips1` |
| CapCut draft generation | Precisely trim materials, call capcut-mate to generate CapCut drafts that can be further edited |
| One-click video output | Chain "AI clipping → draft → (optional) video generation," suited for fast batch output |
| AI + manual collaboration | After AI produces segments, manually adjust `clips1`, then run draft tasks separately |

### Typical Workflow

```text
Import live stream material
  → ASR transcription / summary
  → Create editing project (material + prompt, optional rough selection `clips0`)
  → Path A: one-click output (AI clipping + draft + optional video)
  → Path B: AI clipping → manual refinement…
```

It only does what a music player should: search, organize, continuous playback, and cross-device sync.

## Security

> [!IMPORTANT]
> BiliMusic is for learning and exchange only and must not be used for **any** commercial purpose. All data and documentation come from publicly available internet resources. This project does not perform any reverse engineering, modification, or cracking.
>
> BiliMusic only provides audio playback and does not provide any audiovisual content. Music and video copyrights belong to their original authors. Please respect copyright and use content reasonably.

---

Mainstream Bilibili clients are full video platforms, which are not friendly to people who just want to listen to audio: background playback is restricted, playlist features are weak, and the cross-device experience is fragmented. BiliMusic treats Bilibili as a music content source and focuses only on listening.

Yuuyuko-uu/dsh-fish-buddy.body:
# Fish Buddy

A little whale widget on your desktop + a DSH plugin. The widget handles listening, seeing, and speaking (voice, co-watching subtitles, in-game danmaku, screenshots). The plugin connects it to a conversation session you bind it to: what the widget says goes into that session, and the replies from that session are sent back to the widget.

This repository contains **both halves**:

| Directory | What it is |
|---|---|
| `app/` | Desktop widget (Python + tkinter, packaged as a single-file exe) |
| `lib/` | DSH plugin (host side + settings page) |
| `tests/` | Tests for the plugin and the program |

> ⚠️ **Two version numbers, don't mix them up**: `app/` is the widget program and `lib/` is the DSH plugin. Each is versioned independently, so they are not the same number.
> - Current versions: see `app/version.py` and `package.json`. The README **intentionally doesn't hardcode them**, so it doesn't need updating on every release.
> - What changed: see `CHANGELOG.md`. Entries start with either Program or Plugin.
> - Downloads: see [Releases](https://github.com/Yuuyuko-uu/dsh-fish-buddy/releases) (the exe asset names include the version number).

## What the plugin half does

1. Opens a port on the local machine (default `127.0.0.1:8777`) to receive messages sent by the widget;
2. Sends each message **into the conversation session you bound** (equivalent to you saying it in that session);
3. When the other side finishes a round, sends the reply **back to the widget** (POST to the callback address you entered);
4. When it receives a screenshot or game frame, sends the **image itself** into the session (saved as an attachment first, then referenced);
5. The settings page shows whether the port is reachable, how many messages have arrived, what happened recently, and the last line the character said.

## Asset notes

The character art, speech bubble frames, and danmaku frames in `app/assets/` are distributed with the program and **are not separately licensed for secondary use**. `app/assets/ocr/` contains PP-OCRv6 detection and recognition models (Apache-2.0), and `app/assets/字体/` contains the ZCOOL KuaiLe font (free for commercial use).

## How to configure after installing

**First, install the plugin** (it is already published to npm, so no git is needed):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-fish-buddy
```

> You can also view this package directly on npm, including past versions: <https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-fish-buddy>

After installing, **restart DSH once**. Download the widget's exe separately from [Releases](https://github.com/Yuuyuko-uu/dsh-fish-buddy/releases).

gaoyia/ffrm.body:
# ffrm

ffrm is short for "file force rm," meaning forcibly delete a file.

A Windows and macOS tool. It shows which process is holding a local file or folder, releases that hold, and then deletes it.

Run it with no arguments, or pass a path directly, to open the desktop window. `status`, `unlock`, and `delete` are command-line commands. `mcp` starts a service for editor integrations. The desktop app, the command line, and MCP are the same program.

## Download

Installers are published on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/gaoyia/ffrm/releases). The download page is [gaoyia.github.io/ffrm](https://gaoyia.github.io/ffrm/). The Windows installer is `ffrm-setup.exe` and installs to the current user's directory. The macOS installer is `ffrm.dmg`, built for Apple silicon. After opening it, drag `ffrm.app` into Applications. Portable builds are still published: `ffrm.exe` for Windows and `ffrm` for macOS. In-app updates replace the running program file; they do not download an installer.

If Rust is already installed, you can run:

```text
cargo install ffrm
```

After installing, run `ffrm` in the command line.

## License and Donations

This repository is released under the MIT license. The full text is in `LICENSE`.

The executable is at `target\release\ffrm.exe`. The build copies the MIT license to `target\release\LICENSE`. On macOS, the executable is `target/release/ffrm`.

kuangxing6367/zcbot.body:
# ZCBOT

**A generalized IM platform: a protocol-agnostic, event-driven bot framework**

Minimal kernel · extension-point contracts · official plugin set · business logic lives in your own plugins

[Gitee (China)](https://gitee.com/liquanfeng123/zcbot) ｜
[GitHub (International)](https://github.com/kuangxing6367/zcbot) ｜
[PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/zcbot/) ｜
[Changelog](https://gitee.com/liquanfeng123/zcbot/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) ｜
[LLM Index](https://gitee.com/liquanfeng123/zcbot/blob/main/LLM.md)

---

ZCBOT is a bot framework that is **not bound to any chat protocol**. The kernel only handles event dispatch, plugin loading, permissions, and persistence; protocol adapters, the Web admin console, multi-turn sessions, scheduled tasks, and LLM capabilities are all optional plugins. Swap in a different adapter to connect another IM, or connect to no platform at all and only run scheduled tasks or receive HTTP events.

It goes beyond "it runs" to "it runs stably over the long term": a single-instance lock, crash guard, safe mode, platform-level dependency diagnostics, and security reminders in the Web admin console are all there to back production deployments, not just to provide a scaffold.

## Core Features

1. 🧩 **Protocol-agnostic kernel**: the kernel contains no protocol implementation; OneBot 11 is just one of the default adapters.
2. 🔌 **Pluggable adapters**: built in are OneBot 11, QQ Official, Telegram, Discord, outbound WS, and HTTP injection / HTTP API.
3. 🪝 **Extension point (Hook) system**: can attach to startup/shutdown, Web requests, event dispatch, command execution, protocol actions, and nearly every other runtime stage.
4. 🔥 **Hot-loaded plugins**: drop a plugin into `plugins/` and it takes effect; use decorators to declare commands, permissions, and scheduled tasks.
5. 🖥️ **Web admin console**: Vue 3 + Element Plus; manage plugins, users, permissions, logs, and the database in one place.
6. 🔐 **Permissions and tokens**: node-based permission engine + API tokens (API Keys), with fine-grained control down to the command level.
7. ⏱️ **Multi-turn sessions / scheduled tasks**: session state and the scheduler are official plugins, enabled as needed.
8. 🗄️ **Dual-dialect database**: SQLite works out of the box with zero configuration; switch to MySQL with one step for larger deployments.

Simplified Chinese · [English](https://github.com/m5agent/m5stack-esp-emulator/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

Run M5Stack firmware in a browser or local service to observe the screen, operate buttons and touch, integration-test the covered peripherals, and save reviewable runtime evidence.

timcsy/semorphe.description: One program, three views: code, flowchart, and blocks. Edit any side and the others update instantly!
timcsy/semorphe.body: --- Paste real C++ or Python into it, and it turns into blocks. Drag a block and the code changes with it. Switch to the flowchart and it draws the same program. 🔴 **All three sides are entry points, not "one editable + two read-only"**: ``` You edit the code → blocks and flowchart change on the spot You edit the blocks → code and flowchart change on the spot You edit the flowchart → code and blocks change on the spot ``` Not a "convert" button, and not an update only on save. **While you type, the other two sides are already moving.** Type a piece of C++ → all three sides grow at once → edit once in the code, once in the blocks, once in the flowchart, and the other two sides follow on the spot → press Run, and it really runs ## How it differs from other block tools Most block tools are **one-way**: blocks can become code, but code can't turn back into blocks. A few that are two-way (for example MakeCode) can't go back once you step outside the subset they support. Semorphe aims to do something else: | | | |---|---| | **All three views are editable, and live** | Edit **any** of code, flowchart, or blocks, and the other two catch up on the spot. Not a "convert" button, and not an update only on save | | **Works with real code** | Paste a `.cpp` or `.py` file from your own project, not a toy subset | | **When it can't parse, it says so** | Unrecognized syntax is **not dropped and not guessed**. It becomes a gray block with the original text kept inside, untouched | The third point doesn't sound like a selling point, but it is: **it guarantees the tool won't quietly break your files.** An unrecognized goto becomes a block showing the original text → change a number elsewhere → it doesn't touch a single character of it ## 🔴 The blocks live inside the Arduino IDE, not in a separate program This is Arduino IDE 2.3.8 itself. On the left is its own editor; the middle and right are **Arduino + block tools almost always live outside the Arduino IDE:** | Shape | Examples | |---|---| | Another website | Tinkercad Circuits · Wokwi · Ardublockly | | Another desktop program | mBlock · S4A (Scratch for Arduino) | | A tool plugin for the IDE | ArduBlock (Arduino IDE 1.x, which still opens a **separate window**) | The common thread is the same: **the blocks aren't in the editor you're actually using**. So the workflow goes like this: assemble over there → export `.ino` → switch back to Arduino IDE → upload. And every "→" costs something: ``` Two programs, two files; you have to remember which side you changed, and when you get it wrong, nobody tells you Uploading means switching windows; a student's attention has to move house every time Libraries / boards / serial ports… ```

Progress: **39/105*** 🏗️ For a better reading experience, please see the version on [GitHub Pages](https://xieby1.github.io/nix_config/). ## Table of Contents * [Introduction to Nix/NixOS](#nixnixos简介) * [xieby1 and Nix/NixOS](#xieby1和nixnixos) * [xieby1's Nix/NixOS Configuration](#xieby1的nixnixos配置) * [Folder Structure](#文件夹结构) * [How to Use nix Scripts](#nix脚本的使用方法) * [nix-shell Example](#nix-shell的例子) * [How to Use the nix Configuration](#nix配置的使用方法) * [References](#引用) # Introduction to Nix/NixOS Nix is a *reproducible* package manager and also a *purely functional* programming language. In theory, the Nix package manager can be installed on any Linux distribution (such as Ubuntu, Debian, and Arch) and coexist with that distribution's original package managers (such as snap, apt, and pacman). NixOS, on the other hand, is a Linux distribution managed entirely by the Nix package manager. Nix/NixOS adopts the concept of “Package”, abstracting the Linux kernel, drivers, libraries, user programs, configuration files, and many other aspects. This is similar to how the Linux kernel abstracts devices, disk files, pipes, and more as files. This abstraction allows Nix/NixOS to manage all packages in a unified way. To prevent “packages” from being modified by users intentionally or unintentionally (that is, to guarantee reproducibility), Nix/NixOS places all packages in a read-only file system (mounted at the `/nix/store` directory). Packages in this directory can only be added, modified, or removed through the Nix package manager and the Nix language. To place the files in `/nix/store` where they belong (for example, if a package used by a user contains a `bin/` directory, all files in `bin/` should be placed in `/run/current-system/sw/bin/`), Nix/NixOS makes extensive use of symbolic links. The characteristics of Nix/NixOS described above differ enormously from those of traditional Linux distributions. This gives Nix/NixOS a very steep learning curve. However, once you adapt to these characteristics, it can greatly improve engineering efficiency! # xieby1 and Nix/NixOS For many years, Nix/NixOS has been an important foundation for my study and work, mainly in the following areas: * Learning Linux.
